title: Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
text: Probability Direction (pd) often used decision rule: hypothesis accepted pd exceeds threshold. decision made repeatedly across several hypotheses, family-wise error probability can much higher intended. pd.adjust() addresses problem making implicit prior probability global null explicit, following prior-odds framework Jeffreys (1938) Westfall et al. (1997). global prior probability hypotheses null, q, decomposed per-hypothesis prior: P(H0)=q1/mP(H_0) = q^{1/m} pd reweighted Bayes’ theorem: pdadj=pdP(H1)pdP(H1)+(1−pd)P(H0)pd_{\text{adj}} = \frac{pd P(H_1)}{pd P(H_1) + (1 - pd) P(H_0)} prior conservative ( P(H0)>P(H1)P(H_0) > P(H_1) ), adjustment always shrinks pd toward lower bound. parameters correlated, effective number tests meffm_\text{eff} (Cheverud, 2001) used place m, producing less conservative adjustment. function supports two testing modes, can mixed across hypotheses within call: Direction-agnostic (direction = "two.sided"): pd = max⁡(Pr⁡(θ̂>θnull),Pr⁡(θ̂<θnull))\max\big(\Pr(\hat\theta > \theta_\text{null}),\, \Pr(\hat\theta < \theta_\text{null})\big), bounded [0.5,1][0.5, 1] construction; pdadjpd_\text{adj} also floored 0.50.5. Directional (direction = "greater" "less"): pd raw one-sided posterior probability predicted side, [0,1][0, 1]. Values 0.50.5 indicate posterior concentrated opposite predicted direction; adjustment shrink values, reflecting combined weight data conservative prior hypothesis.

title: Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
code: library(multibayes)  # From a vector of pd values (independence assumed, direction-agnostic) pd_values <- c(H1 = 0.999, H2 = 0.946, H3 = 0.813, H4 = 0.763, H5 = 0.891, H6 = 0.987) pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, q = 0.4)  # Simulate posterior draws Sigma <- matrix(0, nrow = 6, ncol = 6); diag(Sigma) <- 1 mu    <- c(1, -0.1, 0.8, 0, 2, 3) draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(n = 4000, mu = mu, Sigma = Sigma) colnames(draws) <- c("H1", "H2", "H3", "H4", "H5", "H6")  # From posterior draws pd.adjust(draws = draws, q = 0.4, null.value = 0)  # Mix of directional and agnostic tests with parameter-specific nulls pd.adjust(draws = draws, q = 0.4, null.value = c(0.2, 0, 0.2, 0, 0.5, 0.5),            direction = c("greater", "two.sided", "greater", "two.sided",             "greater", "greater"))

title: Prior-odds adjustment for Probability of Direction (pd) — pd.adjust
text: pd Numeric vector pd values. direction-agnostic tests, values must \([0.5, 1]\). directional tests, values raw one-sided probabilities \([0, 1]\). Ignored draws supplied. draws Optional matrix data frame posterior draws (columns = parameters). provided, pd values computed automatically draws according direction null.value. q Numeric scalar \((0, 1)\). prior probability hypotheses null simultaneously. null.value Numeric scalar vector. null (reference) value posterior evaluated, specified scale posterior. single scalar applies null parameters; vector length ncol(draws) assigns distinct null parameter. Ignored pd supplied directly. Defaults 0. direction Character vector "greater", "less", "two.sided" (NULL). Specifies testing mode hypothesis: "greater" positive directional test (\(\Pr(\theta > \theta_\text{null})\)), "less" negative directional test (\(\Pr(\theta < \theta_\text{null})\)), "two.sided" direction-agnostic testing (maximum sides). scalar recycled match number parameters; mixed vector allows different modes across hypotheses. Defaults NULL (direction-agnostic parameters).

title: Prior-odds adjustment for Probability of Direction (pd) — pd.adjust
text: data.frame one row per hypothesis, containing: pd (values used adjustment), pd.adj (adjusted values), q (prior probability global null), m (number tests), qm (prior probability null test). direction-agnostic tests, pd pd.adj bounded \([0.5, 1]\); directional tests, \([0, 1]\), values \(0.5\) indicating data (adjustment) favoured opposite direction. draws supplied, output additionally includes mean.est (posterior mean per parameter), null.value (null reference values), direction.

title: Prior-odds adjustment for Probability of Direction (pd) — pd.adjust
text: adjustment follows Bayes' theorem. Given per-hypothesis prior \(P(H_0) = q^{1/m}\) complement \(P(H_1) = 1 - P(H_0)\), adjusted pd : $$    pd_{adj} = \frac{pd P(H_1)}{pd P(H_1) + (1 - pd) P(H_0)} $$ prior conservative (\(P(H_0) > P(H_1)\)), adjustment always shrinks pd toward lower bound. Direction-agnostic tests ("two.sided"): pd defined \(\max\!\big(\Pr(\hat\theta > \theta_\text{null}),\, \Pr(\hat\theta < \theta_\text{null})\big)\) bounded \([0.5, 1]\) construction. \(pd_{adj}\) also floored \(0.5\), adjustment produces shrinkage toward \(0.5\). Directional tests ("greater" "less"): pd raw posterior probability mass predicted side, \(\Pr(\hat\theta > \theta_\text{null})\) \(\Pr(\hat\theta < \theta_\text{null})\), defined \([0, 1]\). Values pd \(0.5\) indicate posterior concentrated opposite predicted direction; adjustment shrink values toward \(0\), reflecting combined weight data conservative prior hypothesis. Mixed use directional direction-agnostic tests within call supported: element direction handled independently, prior-odds adjustment applied uniformly across hypotheses regardless directionality.
